subject: Servability playbook: batching, cache, quantization proposal
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alice Cheng <alice@brightleaf.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Servability playbook: batching, cache, quantization proposal

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I put together a short "servability playbook" draft that highlights practical levers to hit your 150ms p50 streaming target while keeping token cost under control for your chat use case. The attached deck focuses on three short-term levers we can pilot in parallel:

- Continuous batching with latency windows (micro-batching for 1–2ms gain vs cost)
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and user intents
- Two quantization profiles + model variant routing (4-bit fast vs 8-bit quality)

Key tradeoffs in the doc: concurrency limits that affect throughput vs burstability, and where graceful fallback to a slightly smaller model helps keep the UI snappy under traffic spikes. I also included an ops checklist for smoke tests and a small cost estimate table based on your traffic profile (100k messages/day).

Attachments: servability-playbook-v1.pdf, latency-test-results-20270618.csv

As next steps I propose:
1) Pilot: run a 2-week pilot enabling cache + 4-bit quant on a subset of traffic (10% prod)
2) Performance runbook: schedule a short load window next Tue to validate p50/p90 with batching knobs
3) Decision review: align on whether to adopt the 4-bit fast profile or fallback to 8-bit for quality-sensitive intents

Can you confirm: (a) a 10% pilot window works for you next week, and (b) do you have any compliance blockers for storing KV cache for 48h?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Alice Cheng <alice@brightleaf.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Servability playbook: batching, cache, quantization proposal

Kim — thanks for the recap and the materials. A couple quick clarifying questions before we lock pilot dates: 

1) For the 10% pilot, do you recommend a sampling strategy (user-id bucketing vs session-based)? We prefer session-based but concerned about cold-starts.
2) For KV caching: BrightLeaf policy allows ephemeral caching for 72h but we need to avoid persistent storage of PII. Are you suggesting we cache prompts only (system & user-intent fingerprints) or full user messages?
3) Any special telemetry we should add to our side to make validation faster?

Also, FYI we have a product review on Tue afternoon (2pm PT). If we can validate the perf window earlier in the day that would help.

-Alice
VP Product, BrightLeaf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alice Cheng <alice@brightleaf.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Servability playbook: batching, cache, quantization proposal

Alice — great questions. Short answers up top, details below.

1) Sampling strategy: recommend session-based bucketing for UX consistency; to mitigate cold-starts we suggest a short warm-up burst (5% of sessions) routed to the same model variant during the first 30s. This keeps the cache hit-rate stable.

2) KV caching scope: cache only non-PII fingerprints and system prompts. We will compute deterministic hashes on your side before sending keys to the cache. We will not store raw user messages. I noted this in the playbook appendix (see proposal-appendix.md).

3) Telemetry: please add the following event-level markers:
   - redwood.batch_latency_ms (per-batch)
   - redwood.kv_hit (boolean) with key_type tag (system|intent)
   - redwood.model_variant (fast|quality)

Perf window timing: we can run the validated load test Tue 11:00–12:30 PT (earlier than your 2pm review). That should give you time to digest results.

Attached: updated pilot checklist (inlined into servability-playbook-v1.pdf) and a sample latency CSV with synthetic runs (latency-test-results-20270618.csv).

What we'll measure during the pilot: p50/p90/p99 streaming latency, token unit cost, model fallback rate, and a small quality check via a 200-case prompt set you can vote on.

If that all sounds good I'll loop engineering to schedule the pilot change (feature flag + routing) and create a short mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Cheng <alice@brightleaf.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Servability playbook: batching, cache, quantization proposal

Looping in execution owners and adding a couple pragmatic notes: 

- Engineering note on batching: we'll implement continuous batching with a 8ms soft-window and 25ms hard-window so we can trade a small p50 delta for throughput. Default config will be 8ms; for the pilot we can expose the window as a flag.
- Fallback routing: we'll add a simple token-cost threshold rule so that when cost-per-request rises 20% above baseline we route to the 4-bit fast variant for 15s windows, then re-evaluate.
- Rollback plan: feature flag off + instantaneous model pin back to current prod variant.

Action items assigned: 
1) Ben: implement batching flag and fallback rule in the staging cluster by Mon EOD (2027-06-21).
2) Karthik: prepare rollout playbook and SLA/backstop notes for exec review.
3) Kimberly/Marissa: finalize pilot MRP and QA prompt set; Kimberly to push final doc to Drive.

Alice/Tom: can you confirm the 11:00–12:30 PT slot on Tue for the load window? If yes we'll schedule and share a short runbook link.

Ben Carter
